subject: Aurora Health onboarding — model shortlist, context & token profile
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Aurora Health onboarding — initial model shortlist & token profiling

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation I pulled together a short model shortlist and an initial token/context profile to help the implementation team size capacity and estimate cost. I attached a quick spreadsheet (aurora_token_profile.xlsx) with the sample traffic breakdown you shared plus my derived estimates. TL;DR below and then a few questions.

TL;DR
- Recommended shortlist for POC: 1) Llama2-13B (quantized 8-bit), 2) Mistral-Instruct-7B (FP16), 3) RedOpt-7B-ctx6k (if you want a Redwood-verified variant).
- Peak concurrency to plan for (POC): 12–18 r/s across the service (burst to 30r/s expected on billing cycle alerts).
- Token profile: avg request tokens ~300, avg response tokens ~420, 90th pct response ~1,200, 99th pct ~5,800 — we should plan for context windows up to 6,144 for edge cases.
- Recommended starting runtime config: dynamic batching with max_batch_ms=15, max_tokens=8192 per batch, prefix caching for repeated prompts.

Questions for you:
1) Can you confirm the proportion of requests that include patient longitudinal notes vs short metadata-only prompts? (spreadsheet assumes 18% long-note).
2) Any regulatory requirement to keep model/context out of the cloud regions? If so we’ll route to Dedicated/Private.

Next steps I propose: I’ll loop in Karthik (implementation) and Rishi (AE) to create a mutual action plan and a kickoff for implementation next week. If you want a narrower POC scope we can also restrict to two endpoints (short chat and long-note summarization).

Attachments: aurora_token_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet) — sample traffic + token histograms

Best,
Monica Patel

Thanks for this — the spreadsheet looks very helpful. Quick answers:
- Long notes (full patient encounter text) are about 22% of traffic, not 18 — these are from our intake portal and batch ingestion (we didn’t call that out well on the call).
- We do have an internal rule that PHI content must not leave our VPC unless it’s tokenized/anonymized; for the POC we can run a shuffled/anonymized sample in Redwood Hosted, but production will have to be Private or Dedicated.
- Peak bursts: when we run end-of-day report generation we see spikes up to 28 r/s sustained for ~3–4 minutes.

Can we schedule a technical kickoff with Karthik next Tue or Wed morning PST? Also please share the recommended batching settings — our infra team will want to see the math.

Subject: Fwd: Aurora Health onboarding — initial model shortlist & token profiling

Hi Karthik / Rishi — forwarding Samira's confirm and the spreadsheet. Key points from the customer that affect sizing and model choice:

Summary (customer-confirmed)
- Long-note traffic: 22% of requests (avg request tokens 1,800 when long).
- Burst behavior: up to 28 r/s sustained for a few minutes; baseline POC expected 12–18 r/s.
- PHI policy: production must be Private or Dedicated; POC can be hosted with anonymized samples.

Implementation asks (please action):
1) Karthik — propose an initial Redwood deployment topology for the POC (hosted vs dedicated hybrid), quoting expected GPU footprint and recommended model variant(s). Please include: per-GPU QPS for each shortlisted model, expected token/sec throughput, and plan for autoscaling during 30r/s bursts.
2) Rishi — I'll need a quick draft mutual action plan for Samira (2–4 week POC timeline, success criteria, data/ingest gating).
3) Everyone — review the attached aurora_token_profile.xlsx (I added a column with cost delta estimates between Llama2-13B q8 and Mistral-7B FP16).

Initial internal recommendation (monica's opinion):
- POC: Mistral-Instruct-7B (FP16) as primary for latency-sensitive endpoints; Llama2-13B (q8) as fallback for long-note summarization where larger context helps. If we can provision RedOpt-7B-ctx6k (Redwood-verified 6k context build), that reduces cost for long-note throughput.
- Batching: start with max_batch_ms=15, max_inputs_per_batch=64 for Mistral; for Llama2-13B q8 use max_batch_ms=30 and max_inputs_per_batch=32 because of per-token cost/temp memory.
- Cache: enable prefix caching for standard extraction prompts (saves ~18% token cost in our estimate).

Attachments included: aurora_token_profile.xlsx, model_shortlist_readme.pdf, implementation-checklist.md

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/5421) and onboard folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AuroraOnboardDocs)

Monica

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Aurora Health onboarding — initial model shortlist & token profiling

Thanks Monica — I reviewed the spreadsheet and put rough sizing below for the POC (narrow scope: short chat + long-note summarize endpoints).

Sizing estimate (POC) — conservative:
- Baseline traffic: 15 r/s average (peak bursts to 28 r/s)
- Token/sec estimate (avg): (15 r/s) * (avg in+out tokens 720) = ~10,800 tokens/sec
- Long-note windowing: when 22% are long (avg tokens 1,800) token/sec increases to ~16,500 during those minutes.

Model per-GPU throughput (approx):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B FP16: ~14–18k tokens/sec on A100-80GB with optimized kernels (single model per GPU with room for batching). Latency P95 ~220ms for avg prompt; scales well with batching.
- Llama2-13B q8: ~9–12k tokens/sec on A100-80GB; better single-request quality for long-context but higher memory footprint. P95 ~420–650ms depending on batch size.
- RedOpt-7B-ctx6k (quantized): ~12–15k tokens/sec on A100-80GB; optimized for 6k contexts with lower cost than FP16 13B.

POC footprint recommendation:
- Run Mistral-7B on 1 GPU for baseline (handles avg traffic with headroom); add 1 standby GPU for burst/failover.
- Provision 1 Llama2-13B q8 instance (or RedOpt-7B-ctx6k if available) for long-note summarization — this can be autoscaled to 2 GPUs during sustained bursts.
- Autoscaling policy: scale on tokens/sec and queue depth; target SLO P95 latency <500ms for short chat. For bursts above 25 r/s for >60s, proactively add the second Llama2 q8 replica.

Batching / config notes:
- max_batch_ms=15 for Mistral endpoints, max_batch_ms=30 for Llama2 q8 summarization.
- Use prefix caching for standardized extraction prompts.
- Enable KV cache reuse for multi-turn sessions (saves ~25% tokens in reuse scenarios).

Next actions I will take this week:
- Build a quick cost/throughput runbook for POC variants (Mistral-only vs hybrid) and share numbers by Fri.
- Schedule a kickoff with Samira (Mon/Wed mornings PST) — propose Tue 2026-11-10 10:00am PST.

Karthik
